basis: The exact brief only; exact plan not released at discovery time.
access_utc_precision_note: UTC timestamps are nearest contemporaneous clock samples for the web retrieval batches; the web tool does not expose a per-page fetch timestamp.
local_evidence_policy: No page copies or downloaded code. sources/README.md is the bounded navigation index; this JSON preserves exact source identities and locators.

sources.title: Language Server Protocol 3.17 specification
sources.version_or_commit: LSP 3.17 specification path; source branch is named gh-pages; no commit SHA observed.
sources.locator: Base protocol, lines 301-348 (cancellation, progress); line 374 (capability exchange during initialize); change log lines 766-768.
sources.observed_behavior: Capabilities are exchanged during initialize. Progress uses a token separate from request IDs. Cancellation is a notification; implementation-dependent messages may be ignored, and a synchronous peer may be unable to react.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: LSP 3.17 base-protocol conditions; cancellation support does not promise preemption or termination.
sources.applicability: Protocol design pattern only; this is not an export-worker standard and must not be presented as one.

sources.title: Linux kernel Control Group v2 documentation
sources.version_or_commit: latest documentation alias; exact kernel documentation revision was not surfaced. Accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Basic Operations/Availability and Enabling (lines 145-173); Resource Distribution Models (210-242); cpu.weight/cpu.max (568-601); memory.max (711-722); io.max (1388-1416); pids.max (1560-1595). Core Interface Files cgroup.kill (lines 480-489).
sources.observed_behavior: Controllers are not enabled by default; availability is conditional on kernel support and no v1 binding. Controllers are enabled top-down. CPU weights distribute to active eligible work; cpu.weight defaults to 100. cpu.max defaults to unlimited. memory.max defaults to max and can invoke the OOM killer; usage may temporarily exceed it. io.max is per device; pids.max is a process count hard limit. cgroup.kill kills the cgroup and descendants via SIGKILL and handles concurrent forks; it exists on non-root cgroups and fails for threaded cgroups.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Host must expose cgroup v2 controllers, enable them in the hierarchy, and delegate configuration rights; weights are not a queue-aging guarantee. Resource controls are hierarchical.
sources.applicability: Linux process-tree resource controls where the editor/service has the required delegation. Not a cross-platform sandbox or an unconditional guarantee.

sources.title: Windows Job Objects
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn Win32 documentation; page last updated 2025-07-14 in retrieved rendering.
sources.locator: Managing Processes in Jobs; Job Limits and Notifications; managing a process tree; JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE.
sources.observed_behavior: Jobs manage associated processes as a unit and can terminate all associated processes. CreateProcess children are included by default, except documented creation paths; breakaway flags can detach descendants. Closing the last handle with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE terminates associated processes.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Nested jobs require Windows 8/Server 2012 or newer; older systems have different constraints. Win32_Process.Create children and configured breakaway are exceptions to default descendant association.
sources.applicability: Windows per-export process-tree lifecycle and containment. Pair with access-control mechanisms; job membership alone does not restrict filesystem access.

sources.title: JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION
sources.version_or_commit: Win32 API documentation; supported client lists Windows XP desktop apps.
sources.locator: ProcessMemoryLimit and JobMemoryLimit members; Remarks; LimitFlags condition.
sources.observed_behavior: With the corresponding JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT flags, a per-process or job-wide limit constrains committed virtual memory; the limits are independent and may be combined. Peak accounting is exposed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Fields are ignored unless the corresponding limit flag is set. This is committed virtual memory, not a blanket promise about resident set size or every host resource.
sources.applicability: Windows memory budgeting for an assigned job object; verify policy and process assignment on supported versions.

sources.title: JOBOBJECT_CPU_RATE_CONTROL_INFORMATION
sources.version_or_commit: Win32 API documentation, last updated 2021-04-02; minimum supported client Windows 8 desktop apps.
sources.locator: ControlFlags; hard cap, weight, minimum/maximum rate; Remote Desktop Services caveat.
sources.observed_behavior: The enabled policy may use a relative weight (1-9, default 5), a hard cap, or min/max rates. A hard cap pauses job threads for the rest of a scheduling interval once reached.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: CPU rate control is unavailable under Remote Desktop Services when Dynamic Fair Share Scheduling is in effect; minimum-rate sums cannot exceed 100%.
sources.applicability: Windows host CPU distribution/budget primitive; it does not provide application queue fairness or prevent starvation by itself.

sources.title: Wasmtime StoreLimitsBuilder
sources.version_or_commit: docs.rs latest resolved to wasmtime 49.0.2 during access.
sources.locator: memory_size and related StoreLimitsBuilder methods.
sources.observed_behavior: A configured memory_size limits each wasm linear memory individually; it defaults to unlimited. Separate limits exist for memories, tables, elements, and instances.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Limit must be installed in the Store's resource limiter; each linear memory gets its own allowance. Does not cap the full Wasmtime process or native host allocations.
sources.applicability: Optional Wasmtime adapter only; not evidence that an OS sandbox label enforces process memory.

sources.title: Wasmtime Config fuel and epoch interruption
sources.version_or_commit: docs.rs latest resolved to wasmtime 49.0.2 during access.
sources.locator: consume_fuel (lines 286-303); epoch_interruption (305-319).
sources.observed_behavior: Fuel can trap when the configured instruction budget is exhausted; fuel starts empty and consume_fuel defaults false. Epoch interruption can yield/trap at checked points; trap is the default deadline behavior, while yielding requires configuration.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Controls are opt-in and apply to WebAssembly execution; fuel is not wall-clock or total-process CPU accounting, and host calls/native code require separate controls.
sources.applicability: Optional compatible-Wasm runtime for deterministic execution budgeting, with OS supervision still needed.

sources.title: Wasmtime WASI WasiCtxBuilder filesystem preopens
sources.version_or_commit: docs.rs latest resolved to wasmtime-wasi 49.0.2 during access.
sources.locator: preopened_dir method and examples; default filesystem access; FsPerms behavior.
sources.observed_behavior: WASI has no filesystem access by default when there are no preopened directories. A host directory can be exposed under a guest path with explicit read-only or read-write permissions; traversal above a preopen is prevented.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Builder defaults include no preopens, but TCP/UDP socket APIs are allowed with all addresses denied. The embedder chooses host paths/permissions; exact behavior must be checked against the selected release.
sources.applicability: Capability-shaped filesystem option for WASI-compatible converters, not native converters in general.

sources.title: Apple: Accessing files from the macOS App Sandbox
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple Developer documentation; no semantic version or commit shown.
sources.locator: Overview; selected-file access; security-scoped URLs; limitations and permissions.
sources.observed_behavior: App Sandbox restricts access to protected resources; open/save panels extend access to selected URLs, with scoped access lifetime. The app's container is writable, but access outside needs capability/authorization and can still be denied by POSIX ACLs or other policy.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Folder selection can extend access recursively; selected executable paths have distinct restrictions. Not all operations are guaranteed by an entitlement.
sources.applicability: macOS file-access policy for editor/sandboxed helper design; reviewed source specifies capabilities rather than per-converter memory quotas.

sources.title: Apple archived App Sandbox child inheritance guidance
sources.version_or_commit: Archived Apple documentation; page predates current OS releases, accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Enabling App Sandbox Inheritance, lines 338-354; child rights and dynamic file access.
sources.observed_behavior: A child may inherit the parent App Sandbox using the specified entitlements; Apple says XPC is preferred for privilege separation and child-process inheritance does not provide XPC's security. Inherited rights are static; files opened after launch must be passed as data or by bookmark.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The child must use exactly the app-sandbox and inherit entitlements for this configuration; user-selected file access acquired dynamically is not inherited automatically.
sources.applicability: macOS helper process trade-off; because page is archived, revalidate against supported deployment OS and current Apple guidance.

sources.title: Pandoc filters documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current Pandoc documentation alias; exact release/commit not fixed on the page.
sources.locator: Pandoc filters overview and JSON executable pipeline (lines 20-44); technical invocation details (275 onward). Security caveat is in separate user manual source S21.
sources.observed_behavior: A JSON filter is an executable pipe that reads/writes JSON AST; embedded Lua is another option and is described as usually faster. The CLI invokes a filter between parsing and writing.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is Pandoc's interface, not a general converter protocol. External filters are executable programs and inherit filesystem risks described by Pandoc's own security note.
sources.applicability: Useful unfamiliar product pattern and performance/compatibility alternative; not a security guarantee.

sources.title: Pandoc 3.8.3 release
sources.version_or_commit: Release 3.8.3; commit 568dab1; retrieved release UI showed '01 Dec 10:30' without a year. The year is not independently inferred.
sources.locator: Release body and API changes; regressions fixed from 3.8, including PDF/WeasyPrint and Typst smart quotes; linked issues #11275 and #11256.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The release UI omitted a year for its displayed Dec 1 time; use the immutable tag/commit as identity and do not infer chronology from the incomplete date.

sources.title: Pandoc issue 11275: SVG and WeasyPrint regression

sources.title: LibreOffice file conversion filter table
sources.version_or_commit: latest Help alias; exact LibreOffice release not exposed in retrieved page.
sources.locator: Usage lines 17-30; columns for API filter name, media type and extension around line 160; PDF/graphic filter entries.
sources.observed_behavior: CLI syntax separates output extension, API filter name, and parameters; filters are identified by names and media types. Last repeated --convert-to option is effective.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Current Help alias can change; filter names and supported parameters depend on the installed LibreOffice release.
sources.applicability: Example of an installed converter's explicit format/filter surface; demonstrates why negotiation must use exact versioned IDs and schemas.

sources.title: Linux rename(2) manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Linux man-pages 6.19, dated 2026-02-08; rename is also specified by POSIX.1-2024.
sources.locator: DESCRIPTION (atomic replacement); ERRORS (EXDEV); BUGS (NFS failure/retry ambiguity).
sources.observed_behavior: Replacing an existing target is atomic for pathname visibility; cross-mounted-filesystem rename fails with EXDEV. NFS may report failure after the server performed the rename.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Linux/POSIX pathname semantics and underlying filesystem; atomic visibility is not the same as crash durability or a transaction over a multi-file bundle.
sources.applicability: Linux same-filesystem local publish primitive; destination adapters must account for cross-volume and network semantics.

sources.title: Windows ReplaceFileW
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn Win32 API page; path rules include Windows 10 version 1607 behavior.
sources.locator: Remarks lines 120-143; error codes for partial replacement; REPLACEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH unsupported; same-volume requirement.
sources.observed_behavior: The function combines replacement steps, preserves attributes/ACLs in supported conditions, and may have partial-failure states; all relevant files must be on the same volume.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Path length behavior depends on Windows version/opt-in. Write-through is unsupported; check return code and GetLastError and do not assume failure means no rename occurred.
sources.applicability: Windows same-volume replacement primitive; destination commit and error recovery still belong to the coordinator.

sources.title: Linux fsync(2) manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Linux man-pages 6.19, dated 2026-02-08; POSIX.1-2024.
sources.locator: DESCRIPTION and ERRORS (file data/metadata flush, directory entry caveat, late NFS/ENOSPC/EDQUOT).
sources.observed_behavior: fsync on a file does not necessarily persist the containing directory entry; a separate directory fsync may be required. Some network filesystems may report storage quota/space failures after a write.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Filesystem and device implement durability semantics; sync success is not a universal guarantee across network/object-storage destinations.
sources.applicability: Linux crash-durability guidance for local file commit; do not confuse durability with successful transfer or artifact verification.

sources.title: Windows AppContainer isolation
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn Win32 documentation, last updated 2025-07-08.
sources.locator: File isolation, network isolation and process isolation, lines 31-47.
sources.observed_behavior: AppContainer isolation is based on least privilege; access to files/registry can be granted narrowly, network access is granular, and process-object isolation limits cross-process influence.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Access is only to granted resources; exact compatibility depends on app type and supported Windows versions. It is an access-control sandbox, not the Job Object resource budget.
sources.applicability: Windows sandbox access-control layer to pair with per-job Job Objects.

sources.title: Linux kernel Landlock: unprivileged access control
sources.version_or_commit: latest kernel documentation alias; exact kernel documentation revision not surfaced. Landlock first introduced in Linux 5.13.
sources.locator: Ruleset enforcement and no_new_privs (lines 205-228); file-descriptor rights (279-282); compatibility/ABI check (283-307); build/boot support (877-883); network access-right ABI introductions (438-468, 843-870).
sources.observed_behavior: Landlock lets a process add an irreversible, additive access policy for itself and subsequent children; per-directory filesystem rules and network rights are explicit. The current thread and inherited file descriptors have conditions that affect coverage.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Linux 5.13+ with CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK built and LSM enabled at boot. Check ABI at runtime; unprivileged enforcement requires no_new_privs. Some rights, network controls and thread synchronization appeared only in later ABIs. Existing file descriptors can retain access granted before enforcement; start in a fresh single-thread worker and close unneeded inherited handles.
sources.applicability: Linux filesystem/network confinement option to pair with cgroup resources; cannot be promised on every kernel/boot configuration.

sources.title: Pandoc User Guide security note
sources.version_or_commit: Current Pandoc User Guide alias; exact release/commit not fixed on the page.
sources.locator: A note on security, lines 4867-4883; filter/custom-writer filesystem capability and --sandbox scope.
sources.observed_behavior: The manual warns filters/custom writers can perform arbitrary filesystem operations; --sandbox affects readers/writers only, and combining it with filters or PDF engines leaves security risks.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Claim is specific to Pandoc sandbox behavior and cited filter/custom-writer extension points; it is not a general sandbox API guarantee.
sources.applicability: Evidence for why an external converter/filter must be treated as executable code and separately contained.
